chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abū Muḥammad al-Wābishī, said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about some people who claimed against a slave a crime that would encompass his neck, and the slave confessed to it.

He عليه السلام said: “The confession of a slave is not valid against his master. So if they establish proof for what they claimed against the slave, they may take the slave on account of it, or his master may ransom him.”

key_terms.أَقَرَّ: he confessed or acknowledged the claim
key_terms.جِنَايَةً: a criminal offense or injurious act giving rise to legal liability
key_terms.سَيِّدِهِ: his master, who holds proprietary authority over the slave
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his master or patron in this legal context
key_terms.يَفْتَدِيَهُ: to ransom him or redeem him by compensation

ai.seo_question: Is a slave’s confession legally valid against his master in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning claims of a criminal offense against a slave. It states that a slave’s confession is not legally effective against the master, and that liability is established only through proof, after which the claimant may take the slave or the master may ransom him.
